headline: All seven majors below the 200-day line; momentum diverging as funding flips negative across alts while Bitcoin longs crowd in.
paragraphs: The regime is downtrend across the board. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, Doge, and ADA are all trading below their 200-day simple moving averages, and none of them have achieved a golden cross. Bitcoin is furthest from its 12-month high at 46.6% below, but Doge sits at 74.5% below, and ADA at 82.0% below. This is not a mixed market; it is a market where the prevailing trend remains lower. The distance matters: ADA and Doge are deep in drawdown territory, while BTC retains more relative altitude. When all seven of the major holdings in the traditional crypto portfolio are below their long-term trend lines, the baseline regime is bearish, and that baseline has not changed.

Momentum tells a different story inside that downtrend, and the split is instructive. Bitcoin and Ethereum both have RSI above 60 (BTC at 62.1, ETH at 65.3) and MACD above the signal line, which means they are registering as overbought relative to their recent range and their momentum is upward. Solana, by contrast, has MACD below the signal line even as RSI sits at 56.1, neutral, which is a mild divergence: price is flat but the oscillator is rolling over. Doge has RSI at 44.4, below 50, yet MACD is above the signal line, suggesting momentum may be ahead of what the price action is showing. The pattern here is a market in which the largest holdings have short-term momentum lift while the alts show cracks in conviction. This matters because momentum divergence in a downtrend can precede either a bounce or a deeper sell-off; the tape itself does not yet declare which.

Positioning reveals the fault line. Bitcoin funding is positive at 0.21% per 8 hours (2.3% annualized), which means longs are paying shorts to hold their bets. The long-to-short ratio is 1.85, indicating a crowded long side. Over the last 18 hours, 1,600 liquidations occurred on Bitcoin, with longs taking 19.4 million dollars in damage and shorts taking 6.9 million, a 3-to-1 asymmetry that favors the short side on the tape. Ethereum has flipped: funding is negative at minus 0.11% per 8 hours (minus 1.2% annualized), and over 16 hours, shorts have been the ones getting flushed out at 10 million dollars versus 5.2 million in long liquidations. Solana, XRP, and Doge all show negative funding, meaning shorts are paying longs, and in each case longs are liquidating more heavily than shorts. This is the tell: Bitcoin is long-biased and expensive to hold, while the altcoin derivatives markets are short-crowded and are being harvested. Open interest is also heavy: Bitcoin at 2.05 billion dollars and Ethereum at 1.36 billion dollars are not trivial sums.

Flows are sending contradictory signals. On ETF flows, Bitcoin saw a redemption of 11.6 million dollars on July 27, and over the last five sessions has seen a net outflow of 204.5 million dollars, with only 3 days of same-direction redemption, which is not yet a firm trend. Ethereum, by contrast, showed an inflow of 11.7 million dollars on July 27 and 77.5 million over the last five sessions, though with only 1 day of same-direction buying, so this is volatile. Whale flows over the past 24 hours show a net movement of Bitcoin off exchanges (2.78 million dollars), but the picture is busy: 139.7 million dollars moved into Coinbase institutional and 119 million into OKEx, while 146.3 million left Coinbase institutional and 115.3 million left Kraken. This is noise layered on signal; the weekly trend over the last four weeks is up 1.34 billion, down 316 million, down 134 million, and up 899 million, which is chop with a slight net positive lean. Stablecoin float sits at 306.4 billion dollars, down 1.34% over 30 days, so dry powder is slowly evaporating.

Fear and Greed stands at 29, squarely in the fear regime, and at the lower end of its 30-day range of 11 to 33. The crowd is scared, yet Bitcoin is long-crowded and Ethereum shorts are being liquidated. This disagreement is the central tension: sentiment is dark, but the actual positioning in the futures markets suggests traders are not yet aligned with that fear. They are instead holding longs in Bitcoin and covering shorts in Ethereum, which is a bet that the regime is bouncing. The tape does not confirm that bet yet; it shows momentum lift in the two largest assets inside a broader downtrend, with alts rolling over, and flows that are mixed and noisy rather than decisive.

Watch for three conditions: a funding flip in Bitcoin, which would signal the long crowd has exhausted its appetite and shorts are beginning to bid. A reclaim of the 200-day line in any of the majors, which would be a regime shift, not just a bounce. And a reversal in the whale weekly trend from the current choppy positive lean into sustained outflow, which would tell you the smart money is lightening up rather than accumulating dips. Until one of those conditions moves, the tape reads as a moment of internal disagreement between the largest holdings and the rest, neither of which has yet broken the downtrend.
